# Every source the research tools can reach (985 of them)

This is the complete list behind `/research` and `/osint`, generated from
the registry the tools actually read. It exists so nobody has to take the
phrase "hundreds of sources" on trust: here they are, with how each one is
reached and how far it can be trusted before anything it says is checked.

**How to read a row.** *Access* is the cheapest free way the tool can query
that source. *Reliability* is a starting assumption about the source itself
— not a grade on any particular claim. Claims are graded separately during
a run, on two axes (see [OSINT-RESEARCH.md](OSINT-RESEARCH.md)); a reliable
source can still carry a wrong claim, which is exactly why the two are
never merged into one score.

### What the access categories mean

- **Open API** — machine-readable, no account, no key, no card
- **Web pages** — no API; predictable public pages the tool can read
- **Paid only** — no free programmatic path — listed so the tool can TELL you it exists
- **Free API key** — free, but you must register for a key
- **Bulk download** — offered as downloadable datasets
- **Search engine** — reached through the private search engine
- **Unclassified** — access method not established

The paid-only entries are kept deliberately. A tool that silently omitted
them would leave you thinking the free sources were everything there is;
instead it can tell you the definitive source exists and sits behind a
subscription, which is a finding in itself.

### Where this list comes from, and how it was checked

The registry was compiled from three curated source lists kept with the
project's design notes, each entry classified by the cheapest free way
to reach it. That classification was then audited against the original
lists rather than assumed correct:

> 2026-08-17: the three curated source lists were re-checked line by line against this registry. 160 names had failed a fuzzy match; classification found 52 were section headings, 23 were variant spellings of entries already present (e.g. WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION = WHO), and 85 were genuine sources missing from the first pass — those were added here. Entries carry a best-known canonical URL or none; no URL was invented.

Sources with no known canonical address carry no link rather than a
guessed one — an invented URL is worse than an absent one.
